summary: DAY structural pass covers all 12 active companies with cumulative lineage and explicit present-vs-future separation. ARM and MU now have enough primary evidence for reproducible substitute/constraint treatment in this lane. The remaining ten retain precise causal-evidence gaps; correlated AI demand is not treated as independent confirmation, and future falsifiers are documented rather than misclassified as current blockers.

evidenceAcquired: Current filing confirms two-engine business structure: launch services plus space systems; Space Systems product revenue materially exceeds launch revenue, reducing single-program dependence at the company level.
unresolvedGaps: GATING after attempt 3: quantify how much durable bottleneck control comes from launch cadence/Neutron versus acquired satellite-component capability and whether competitors can substitute those capabilities without comparable lead time.
falsifiersUnknowns: future falsifier: Neutron delays or reusable-launch competition erodes the launch constraint thesis

evidenceAcquired: Current filing anchors Blackwell Ultra-driven compute/networking expansion and explicit customer concentration; export controls remain a real reachable-market constraint.
unresolvedGaps: GATING after attempt 3: independently compare substitute accelerator economics/software switching costs and quantify dependence on hyperscaler buildout enough to distinguish ecosystem moat from scarcity-cycle rent.
falsifiersUnknowns: future falsifier: custom accelerators plus software portability materially reduce NVIDIA switching costs

evidenceAcquired: Data Center reached 58% of Q2-2026 revenue and current filings show improving gross margin, confirming real demand exposure rather than purely narrative AI optionality.
unresolvedGaps: GATING after attempt 3: primary/independent evidence for software switching cost, accelerator substitution economics and durable share capture is still insufficient.
falsifiersUnknowns: future falsifier: ecosystem friction prevents durable accelerator share despite product performance

evidenceAcquired: Advanced-node manufacturing remains the central physical conversion layer between accelerator design and shipped compute; overseas-fab buildout is the company's main geographic-resilience response.
unresolvedGaps: GATING after attempt 3: quantify resilience/cost tradeoff of overseas capacity and credible advanced-node substitution pathways enough to score scenario robustness rather than simply asserting foundry scarcity.
falsifiersUnknowns: future falsifier: severe Taiwan disruption or faster-than-expected alternative leading-edge capacity

evidenceAcquired: Issuer evidence supports EUV/High-NA lithography as a hard enabling layer for leading-edge logic/DRAM and flags materially lower expected China sales in 2026.
unresolvedGaps: GATING after attempt 3: explicit critical-supplier single-point mapping and practical export/substitution counterfactuals are still not sufficient for reproducible supply-chain-resilience treatment.
falsifiersUnknowns: future falsifier: supplier/export constraints impair system throughput or an alternative patterning path compresses lithography rents

evidenceAcquired: FY2026 filing directly identifies RISC-V as a competitive ecosystem risk; SoftBank control/affiliate economics and customer concentration are quantified; Arm's licensing/royalty model spans multiple end markets without owning fabs.
falsifiersUnknowns: future falsifier: RISC-V/custom ISA adoption materially weakens royalty leverage or SoftBank-related conflicts damage neutral ecosystem positioning

evidenceAcquired: Current filing documents $22B strategic-customer financial commitments, including ~$18B cash deposits, while planning ~$27B FY2026 capex and additional DRAM capacity; this directly captures both present HBM scarcity and the endogenous capacity-response mechanism.
falsifiersUnknowns: future falsifier: industry capacity response outpaces AI-memory demand and collapses scarcity pricing

evidenceAcquired: Issuer history quantifies hyperscaler concentration and current filings confirm cloud/AI networking growth; networking is a second-order beneficiary of accelerated-compute cluster scale.
unresolvedGaps: GATING: present evidence still does not quantify white-box/custom-fabric substitution difficulty and customer-specific re-sourcing risk sufficiently for a reproducible substitution-resilience score.
falsifiersUnknowns: future falsifier: hyperscalers internalize enough fabric/control-plane capability to commoditize merchant switching economics

evidenceAcquired: Five-year Meta agreement up to ~$27B demonstrates demand for dedicated AI compute and links NBIS directly to the GPU/power/datacenter bottleneck stack beginning 2027.
unresolvedGaps: GATING: map GPU procurement/power/interconnection dependencies, contract concentration and substitute capacity from hyperscalers/neoclouds before claiming bottleneck control rather than financed capacity aggregation.
falsifiersUnknowns: future falsifier: abundant competing compute capacity compresses neocloud rents before deployed clusters earn returns

evidenceAcquired: Current filing confirms meaningful customer concentration, consistent with a remote-sensing data business dependent on a relatively small set of institutional/commercial buyers.
unresolvedGaps: GATING: establish why Planet's revisit/data stack is difficult to substitute using competing constellations or sovereign imagery and map which downstream workflows create recurring switching cost.
falsifiersUnknowns: future falsifier: lower-cost competing constellations or public imagery erode data scarcity

evidenceAcquired: Primary evidence anchors three linked capabilities: advanced fission power, fuel/recycling, and radioisotopes; DOE/NRC milestones validate regulatory progress while current filings show capital-intensive pre-scale deployment.
unresolvedGaps: GATING: convert regulatory milestones and customer interest into a sourced causal map of fuel availability, licensing throughput, construction supply chain, grid/interconnection and substitute power economics before claiming durable bottleneck capture.
falsifiersUnknowns: future falsifier: licensing/fuel/construction delays or cheaper firm-power substitutes make Aurora economics noncompetitive

evidenceAcquired: Issuer results show a vertically integrated stack spanning power/datacenters, ASICs, Bitcoin mining and AI Cloud, with growing AI ARR signals but very high capital intensity and leverage.
unresolvedGaps: GATING: separate power/interconnection scarcity advantage from commodity mining economics and prove whether proprietary ASIC/datacenter integration creates durable AI-compute switching cost rather than temporary capacity optionality.
falsifiersUnknowns: future falsifier: AI tenants favor hyperscalers/other neoclouds while mining economics absorb capital and debt capacity

contradictions: AI infrastructure demand simultaneously benefits NVDA, AMD, TSM, ASML, MU, ANET and NBIS; this is one correlated demand complex, not seven independent confirmations.
MU's current scarcity evidence and large customer deposits coexist with an explicit massive capacity-response plan; scarcity rent must be modeled as time-varying rather than permanent.
unknowns: Successor bottlenecks across power, HBM, advanced packaging, networking and interconnection are not yet quantitatively ranked.
Future falsifiers remain unknown outcomes and are not used as present blockers where current causal evidence is otherwise sufficient.
peerRequests: Chief: ARM and MU are structural-causal ready_for_chief; preserve their future falsifiers as monitoring conditions, not gates.
Red Team: attack NBIS/BTDR capital-intensity dependence and OKLO fuel/licensing/construction assumptions.
Discovery: watch for evidence of successor bottleneck migration from GPU scarcity toward power/interconnection, HBM/packaging and network fabrics.
blockingIssues: Ten active companies retain explicit present causal-evidence gaps. ARM and MU are individually ready in this lane; global T0 gate state is outside this lane's promotion authority.
